# Hub: everything in one place

<!-- generated by `npm run hub` (scripts/hub.js) from the repo itself; edit the sources, not this file. Preflight fails when it's stale. -->

One page that points at every skill, spec, check, measure and pitfall in the repo. It is generated from the files it links to, so it can't drift: [scripts/hub.js](../scripts/hub.js) reads them, `npm run hub` rewrites this page, and preflight's **Hub** check fails when it is stale or a link breaks.

**Contents:** [Start here](#start-here) · [Specs](#specs) · [Skills (17)](#skills) · [Subagents (3)](#subagents) · [Spec Kit (9)](#spec-kit-commands) · [Checks (26)](#checks) · [Measures (70)](#measures) · [Tips and pitfalls (43)](#tips-and-pitfalls) · [Where things live](#where-things-live) · [Open decisions](#open-decisions-for-the-humans)

## Start here

- **Who builds with what**: Matt builds with Claude Code; John builds with v0 or Codex ([handoff](../handoff/README.md)). Other agents (the paper watch, helpers) follow the same rules.
- **Rules for every agent**: [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) (Codex and other tools read this one) and [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) (Claude Code). In short: Never push to `main`; Never deploy; Never write agent log entries; No secrets; No Twitter/X; Spec first; Shared documents need both humans; Free tiers only; Real people only as watchlist entries; No co-author trailers; Test data is synthetic.
- **Picking up work**: [handoff/README.md](../handoff/README.md), then [STATE.md](../handoff/STATE.md) (2026-11-07), then an open task under [Specs](#specs), then the [skill](#skills) for the job. Name the REQ IDs in the commit; tick the task in the commit that finishes it.
- **Current project index**: [START_HERE.md](START_HERE.md) links current authority, measurements, app workspaces and audit findings.
- **Before handing work back**: `npm run preflight` (every [check](#checks) below) and `npm test` for bigger changes; report the exact lines ([run-tests](../agent-kit/skills/run-tests/SKILL.md)).
- **Per tool**: Codex [first message](../handoff/prompts/codex.md); v0 [first message](../handoff/prompts/v0.md) and [setup](V0.md); any MCP client loads the skills from [the agent kit](../agent-kit/README.md).

## Subagents

| Subagent | Does |
| --- | --- |
| [significance-reviewer](../agent-kit/agents/significance-reviewer.md) | Reviews how stories are tagged and scored - runs the ontology tagger and significance analysis on given titles or on the sample fixtures, finds mis-tags and mis-ranked stories, and proposes minimal rule changes with unit checks. |
| [source-scout](../agent-kit/agents/source-scout.md) | Researches where to harvest AI-progress news from (journals, proceedings, labs, evaluation orgs, researchers' own blogs, paper searches) and returns ready-to-add catalog entries with each feed's verification status. |
| [verifier](../agent-kit/agents/verifier.md) | Independently checks finished work in this repo - runs preflight, the unit checks and the browser test on SQLite (and Postgres when SQL changed), looks at screenshots, and reports exact pass/fail lines without fixing anything. |

## Spec Kit commands

How a spec is produced: [constitution](../.specify/memory/constitution.md), [templates](../.specify/templates), the prompts we used ([speckit-prompts.md](speckit-prompts.md)) and the [work-from-the-spec](../agent-kit/skills/work-from-the-spec/SKILL.md) skill. Run as `/speckit-<name>` in Claude Code.

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| [/speckit-analyze](../.claude/skills/speckit-analyze/SKILL.md) | Perform a non-destructive cross-artifact consistency and quality analysis across spec.md, plan.md, and tasks.md after task generation. |
| [/speckit-checklist](../.claude/skills/speckit-checklist/SKILL.md) | Generate a custom checklist for the current feature based on user requirements. |
| [/speckit-clarify](../.claude/skills/speckit-clarify/SKILL.md) | Identify underspecified areas in the current feature spec by asking up to 5 highly targeted clarification questions and encoding answers back into the spec. |
| [/speckit-constitution](../.claude/skills/speckit-constitution/SKILL.md) | Create or update the project constitution from interactive or provided principle inputs. |
| [/speckit-converge](../.claude/skills/speckit-converge/SKILL.md) | Assess the current codebase against the feature's spec, plan, and tasks, then append any remaining unbuilt work as new tasks to tasks.md so implement can complete it. |
| [/speckit-implement](../.claude/skills/speckit-implement/SKILL.md) | Execute the implementation plan by processing and executing all tasks defined in tasks.md |
| [/speckit-plan](../.claude/skills/speckit-plan/SKILL.md) | Execute the implementation planning workflow using the plan template to generate design artifacts. |
| [/speckit-specify](../.claude/skills/speckit-specify/SKILL.md) | Create or update the feature specification from a natural language feature description. |
| [/speckit-tasks](../.claude/skills/speckit-tasks/SKILL.md) | Generate an actionable, dependency-ordered tasks.md for the feature based on available design artifacts. |

## Checks

`npm run preflight` runs every check below ([scripts/preflight.js](../scripts/preflight.js); also on `git push` and in [GitHub Actions](../.github/workflows/preflight.yml)). A ✗ fails the run; a ! is a reminder.

| Check | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| JavaScript syntax | Syntax of every JS/MJS file we own |
| JSON files | JSON files parse |
| Bundle builds | json-render bundle builds |
| No secrets | No secrets in tracked files |
| No Twitter/X sources | No Twitter/X sources |
| No Twitter/X in catalog / Content desk / Editorial publishing / Appearance and publishing / Content management / Research foundations / Vocabulary contracts / Entity resolution / Entity grouping / Entity resolution/grouping / Product planning / Term properties / Graph logic / Pipeline quality / Story paging / Pipeline quality / paging / Accuracy paradox guard / Type mappings / Measurement and types / UI dates / Analysis rules | No Twitter/X in the source catalog either; analysis rules behave |
| Modules | kernel boots, boundaries hold, blocks, views and judges are valid |
| Codebase map | every API call a page makes has a route |
| Unslop | UI patterns that read as AI-generated (agent-kit/skills/ui-design) |
| No ignored source files | Nothing the code needs is git-ignored (a fresh clone in CI must have every module file). |
| Naming | Naming convention (docs/NAMING.md): routes, tables, ids, labels, metadata |
| Commit trailers | Commit messages on this branch carry no co-author or session trailers (the humans asked). |
| Commit authors | Commits on this branch are authored by a person, not an assistant identity (the humans asked). |
| Rules and schemas | si-expr (portable rules) and the schema registry: Node vectors, builder/registry units, generated schemas current. |
| Judge edge cases | Judge edge cases (bench/judge-edge-cases.json, proposed REQ-032..REQ-037): a case marked "ok" that breaks fails; known gaps are reported, not failed, so the backlog is visible and can only shrink. |
| Judge properties | Judge fixtures and properties (spec 003, T003-T006): fidelity set shape, near-cutoff report, the Lean model's vectors against review.js, and property tests on 300 generated synthetic texts (known… |
| AGENTS.md | AGENTS.md is what Codex reads (not CLAUDE.md): it must carry the hard rules itself and fit Codex's 32 KiB default. |
| Lab results current | Lab results precomputed for cold starts (scripts/lab-results.js) must match the current examples and runners. |
| Benchmarks | Benchmarks with a ratchet (scripts/bench.js): no metric may get worse than bench/baseline.json allows. |
| Agent kit | skills, subagents, plugin manifests, symlinks, index and MCP handshake |
| Hub | Hub (docs/HUB.md): generated from the repo by scripts/hub.js, so it fails when stale or when a relative link in it breaks (test/hub-unit.js first) |
| Spec trace | every REQ in the shared spec(s) appears in docs/SPEC_TRACE.md, and the trace cites no unknown REQ |
| OpenSpec | OpenSpec beside Spec Kit: generated capability specs current, every REQ mapped, open changes well-formed. |
| Interfaces / Contract | schema or routes changed without docs/INTERFACES.md changing |
| API smoke test | API smoke test on synthetic data (SQLite, random port) |
| Spec acceptance | Spec acceptance (API checks) on the spec version with labelled synthetic sources: every REQ needs a passing check (SC-008). |

## Measures

Benchmarks with a ratchet ([scripts/bench.js](../scripts/bench.js), [bench/README.md](../bench/README.md)): no metric may get worse than [bench/baseline.json](../bench/baseline.json) (updated 2026-11-12) allows. "info" metrics are reported, never failed.

| Metric | Better | Baseline | What it measures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `review.credibility_auc` | higher | 1 | credible items out-rank doubtful ones on credibility |
| `review.score_auc` | higher (tol 0.02) | 0.813 | ...on the guarded score |
| `review.naive_score_auc` | info | 0.281 | ...on the unguarded score (for comparison) |
| `review.verdict_accuracy` | higher | 1 | 'doubtful' or 'withdrawn' exactly when the label says not credible |
| `review.flag_recall` | higher | 1 | share of non-credible items sent to a person |
| `review.flag_false_rate` | lower | 0 | share of credible items sent to a person |
| `review.invariance` | higher | 1 | padding, stuffing, checklists, name-dropping, unbacked claims and injection don't raise the score (96 edits) |
| `review.adversary_gain_guarded` | lower (tol 0.5) | 0 | points the guarded score gains under the attack on the unguarded judge |
| `review.whitebox_gain` | lower (tol 0.5) | 0.25 | points an adversary attacking the guarded score gains |
| `review.adversary_gain_naive` | info | 35.75 | points the same attack gains on the unguarded judge (the attack is real) |
| `review.ms_per_doc` | info | 17.2 | time to review one item |
| `review.fidelity_accuracy` | higher | 1 | paraphrase-fidelity checks right on bench/fidelity-cases.json (52 synthetic pairs: pass/fail and the expected check) |

## Tips and pitfalls

Quoted from the repo's own pitfall, trap, troubleshooting and habits sections (near-duplicates kept once, at their first source). Add new ones there, not here.

**[build-a-page › ui-kit.md](../agent-kit/skills/build-a-page/references/ui-kit.md) › Pitfalls**

- Global rules: `input, select, textarea { width: 100% }` and `.row > * { flex: 1 1 160px }`. Set `width: auto` for inline controls, and don't name your own class `.row`, `.cols`, `.panel` or `.tabs`.
- `[hidden]` is forced to `display: none`; toggle `el.hidden` instead of styles.
- Single-page apps (project page): update the hash with `history.replaceState` and listen for `hashchange`.
- Long tables: wrap in `.tablewrap` so phones scroll the table, not the page.
- The top bar is one line; on phones the nav row scrolls sideways.

**[run-tests › troubleshooting.md](../agent-kit/skills/run-tests/references/troubleshooting.md) › Test troubleshooting**

- `pkill -f serve-fixtures` kills your own shell (exit 144): The pattern matches the command line of the shell running pkill. **Fix:** Anchor it: `pkill -f "^node --no-warnings test/serve-fixtures"`
- `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` on 3200/3300: Server not started yet, or it crashed on boot. **Fix:** `sleep 2` after starting; read its log; a missing module (e.g. a new `lib/*.js` not created yet) crashes boot
- Sign-up in a test script silently fails: Usernames must be at least 3 characters. **Fix:** Use names like `dbguser`
- Drag-and-drop does nothing in Playwright: The drop target is off-screen in a scrolling container. **Fix:** Make the target visible at the test viewport (1200 px wide)
- Navigating to `/page#/other` doesn't re-render: Same document; only the hash changed. **Fix:** The page needs a `hashchange` listener, or use `reload()`
- A `hidden` element still shows: A CSS `display` rule beats the `hidden` attribute. **Fix:** `app.css` has `[hidden]{display:none!important}`; don't override it
- Rows lay out strangely on a new page: Class name collides with an `app.css` class (`.row`, `.cols`, `.panel`, `.tabs`). **Fix:** Use a page-specific name (the project page uses `.irow`)
- Postgres test server: "no response" on 5433: The local cluster stopped with the container. **Fix:** Restart it with `pg_ctl -D <datadir> -o '-p 5433 -k /tmp' start` as a non-root user
- `fixture://` URL refused: `ALLOW_FIXTURE_FEEDS` isn't `1`. **Fix:** Only the sample-data servers set it; never set it in production
- The test catalog shows real sources: `SOURCE_CATALOG` not set. **Fix:** The sample-data servers point it at `test/fixtures/sample-catalog.json`
- Test counts change after adding a fixture source: Feed and filter checks count stories. **Fix:** Add new fixture sources through the admin API late in `e2e.js`, not in `serve-fixtures.js`
- Live feeds fail in the sandbox: The sandbox can't reach most sites. **Fix:** Use fixtures; say plainly that live fetching is unverified
- `waitForSelector('select option')` times out: Options inside a `<select>` are never "visible". **Fix:** Pass `{ state: 'attached' }`
- "registered twice" when a test boots a second kernel: A module kept registry state at file level. **Fix:** Create registries inside `register(env)`
- A module page 404s on Vercel but works locally: `public/m/` wasn't generated. **Fix:** `npm run build` runs `scripts/modules.js gen`; check the build log
- New block doesn't render (blank): Browser registry not regenerated. **Fix:** `npm run build`; `npm run modules:check` reports a stale `client/blocks.gen.jsx`

**[tune-ontology › term-syntax.md](../agent-kit/skills/tune-ontology/references/term-syntax.md) › Known false positives (avoid or work around)**

- `imo`: "IMO" = "in my opinion". **Fix:** Use `imo gold`, `imo problem*`, `international mathematical olympiad`
- `o1`, `o3`: Also appear in unrelated text. **Fix:** Kept for OpenAI, but don't add more two-character terms
- `fair`: Meta's lab vs the word "fair". **Fix:** Existing; don't copy the pattern
- `asi`, `hle`, `aime`: Short acronyms. **Fix:** Only kept where the topic needs them; check on real titles
- `safety`: Very broad. **Fix:** Keep under Safety; don't add more one-word generic terms

**[ui-design › motion.md](../agent-kit/skills/ui-design/references/motion.md) › Always**

- Wrap motion in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, or turn it off under `reduce`. app.css already turns off every token-based animation under `reduce`.
- Animate only `transform` and `opacity` (plus `clip-path` and `filter` for reveals). Never animate `width`, `height`, `top` or `left` on lists.
- Never use `transition: all`.

**[write-portable-sql › sql.md](../agent-kit/skills/write-portable-sql/references/sql.md) › Traps already hit**

- `db.insert` appends `RETURNING id` on Postgres: only use it on tables with an `id` column.
- `pg` returns BIGINT and COUNT as strings unless parsed; `lib/db.js` sets the parser, so don't cast in queries.
- `node:sqlite` is synchronous: `db.tx` serializes transactions, so don't call `db.*` (outside the transaction) from inside `tx(async t => …)`; use `t.*`.
- Ordering by a boolean expression (`x IS NULL`) works on both; ordering by an alias inside `CASE` doesn't on Postgres.
- Postgres is strict about `GROUP BY`: every selected non-aggregate column must be grouped.

**[docs/DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md) › Troubleshooting**

- "To link this repository, check that your Vercel GitHub App has access": Step 1 not done, or done on the wrong account. **Fix:** Matt grants the Vercel app access to the repo
- API returns 500 and logs say `ECONNREFUSED` or `password authentication failed`: No database connected to that environment. **Fix:** Storage → connect Neon to Production/Preview
- Everyone gets logged out after each deploy: The database is SQLite, not Neon. **Fix:** Check `DATABASE_URL` is set; SQLite can't persist on Vercel
- Sources all show errors: A site blocks the fetch, or its feed URL moved. **Fix:** Fix the URL on the Sources page (admin) or pause that source
- Cron never runs: `CRON_SECRET` missing, or deployment not on production. **Fix:** Add the variable and redeploy

**[docs/V0.md](V0.md) › v0 habits to watch for**

- **Rewriting the stack:** it may try to convert the project to Next.js or add a database client. Say no and point it back at the contract.
- **Inventing API fields:** it may make up fields the API doesn't return. Compare its calls with the API table in [INTERFACES.md](INTERFACES.md).
- **Dropping existing pages** while it builds new ones. Check that `/sources` and `/lists` still work in the preview.
- **Placeholder data:** it may hard-code fake data instead of calling the API. Real data comes only from `/api/stories` and `/api/brief`.
